subject: Science
central_question: How can experiments reveal which materials are magnetic, where a magnet's poles are, how magnets show direction and how their poles interact?
in_scope_units: Natural lodestones, artificial magnets and common magnet shapes and uses
Poles of a magnet and the impossibility of a single isolated pole
Finding directions using a freely suspended magnet and magnetic compass
Constructing a simple magnetic compass with a magnetised needle and cork
Attraction and repulsion between like and unlike magnetic poles
Using repulsion and compass deflection to identify magnetic behaviour
Fun applications of magnets and movement without contact
Safe storage and handling of magnets
banned_topics: Detailed atomic or domain theory of magnetism
Electromagnets, electric motors and electromagnetic induction

known_pitfalls.claim: All metals are attracted by magnets.
known_pitfalls.correction: Iron, nickel, cobalt and some of their combinations are magnetic; many other materials, including many metals, are not attracted.

known_pitfalls.claim: The middle of a bar magnet attracts the most iron filings.
known_pitfalls.correction: The maximum iron filings collect near the two ends or poles.

known_pitfalls.claim: Breaking a magnet can produce a single North pole.
known_pitfalls.correction: North and South poles always occur together, even in the smallest broken piece.

known_pitfalls.claim: Attraction proves that an unknown metal bar is a magnet.
known_pitfalls.correction: An iron bar is attracted by both poles; repulsion is the reliable identifying property of a magnet.

recommended_example_progression: Predict, test and classify magnetic and non-magnetic materials.
Locate poles and establish the north-south direction of a freely suspended magnet.
Construct and test a simple compass.
Reason about attraction, repulsion and identifying poles.
Show magnetic action through non-magnetic materials.
